title: Fixture: founder interview on burnout and fundraising

segments.text: Welcome back to the show. Today I'm sitting down with a founder who raised a seed round in three weeks and then almost quit.
Thanks for having me. Yeah, the three weeks part sounds great until you hear what happened after.
So walk me through it. You close the round, money's in the bank, and what, you just stopped sleeping?
Pretty much. Here's the thing nobody tells you: raising money doesn't reduce pressure, it multiplies it. Every dollar is a promise to someone.
I remember sitting in the office at 2am thinking, I have eighteen months of runway and zero idea what to build next week.
That's the part people don't post about on LinkedIn. What did you actually do?
I fired myself as CEO for a week. Literally. I told my cofounder, you make every decision, I'm going to go talk to twenty customers and not open Slack.
And those twenty conversations changed the roadmap completely. We killed the feature we'd raised the round on.
Wait, you killed the thing investors gave you money to build?
Yes. And every single investor said the same thing: we invested in you, not the slide. Which is a cliché until it saves your company.
What's your advice to a founder who's in that 2am moment right now?
Burnout isn't from working too much. It's from working on things you don't believe in. Fix what you're working on before you fix your calendar.
